content.title: Boundary Enforcement | Baseline, Interruption, Correction, Return
content.summary: Establish a formal setting and a clear boundary keeper, use group reactions to localize one interruption, then let the keeper leave the anchor, perform one visible corrective action, and return so the original order resumes in a newly stable state.

quick_start.input_format: formal group baseline and keeper anchor + reaction-localized interruption + single offending object + attributable correction + compositional return
quick_start.recommended_input: In an original glass museum-conservation lab, a senior conservator in a cobalt coat stands on a white floor mark while six technicians face a dim artifact projection. One visitor beacon flashes amber; the conservator seals it inside a black isolation box and returns to the same mark as the projection steadies.
required_anchors: Establish one formal group baseline, one boundary keeper and the keeper's anchor position before the interruption.
Localize exactly one disturbance through spatially connected group reactions before revealing its source.
Use one clear, attributable corrective action that removes or neutralizes the source without adding a second conflict.
Return the keeper to the original anchor and repeat enough of the opening composition to prove restored order.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish a formal setting and a clear boundary keeper, use group reactions to localize one interruption, then let the keeper leave the anchor, perform one visible corrective action, and return so the original order resumes in a newly stable state.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish a formal group setting, a stable boundary keeper and one readable baseline rule. Introduce a single localized interruption through synchronized reactions before revealing its physical source. Let the same keeper leave the anchor position, perform one attributable corrective action, then return to the repeated baseline composition with a restrained state change. The reusable mechanism is reaction-localized interruption, visible enforcement and compositional return, not the source religious costume, chapel, phone, violent gesture or exact joke.

invariants.rule: Establish one formal group baseline, one boundary keeper and the keeper's anchor position before the interruption.
invariants.purpose: Defines the rule and who can enforce it.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a stable baseline, the intervention reads as random aggression.

invariants.rule: Localize exactly one disturbance through spatially connected group reactions before revealing its source.
invariants.purpose: Creates anticipation while preserving understandable geography.
invariants.ablation_failure: A detached reaction montage cannot identify where the problem occurs.

invariants.rule: Reveal one physical source of interruption and keep it traceable to the same location or participant.
invariants.purpose: Turns social tension into an inspectable cause.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing the offending object or location breaks accountability.

invariants.rule: Use one clear, attributable corrective action that removes or neutralizes the source without adding a second conflict.
invariants.purpose: Provides a decisive payoff and keeps the mechanism compact.
invariants.ablation_failure: Multiple attacks, arguments or unrelated gags dilute the boundary action.

invariants.rule: Return the keeper to the original anchor and repeat enough of the opening composition to prove restored order.
invariants.purpose: Closes the loop through visual evidence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on the removed object or crowd reaction leaves the formal state unresolved.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source veiled religious figure, black-and-white habit, face paint, cross and altar identity
the source stone chapel, candles, funeral-like black clothing and attendee faces
the source handheld phone, throat-level gesture, boot action and window ejection gag
the source exact reaction order, aisle blocking, compositions and final smile
any source logos, device marks, religious symbols, implied identities or exact sound cues
